step: Implement Data Models, Repositories, and Basic DB Entity Relationships for Freelancer and Project
sub_steps: Create Freelancer entity with required fields (id, name, email (unique), skills, hourlyRate, bio, joinedDate) and validation annotations.
Create Project entity with required fields and relationship with Freelancer (assignedFreelancer, nullable). Enum for status. Appropriate validation annotations.
Configure bidirectional (if necessary) or unidirectional relationships using jakarta.persistence annotations.
Create FreelancerRepository interface with: findBySkillsContaining (case-insensitive, matches any skill, possibly using @Query annotation), findByHourlyRateLessThanEqual.
Create ProjectRepository interface with: findByStatus, findByBudgetGreaterThanEqual, findByClientName (all using appropriate query derivations or @Query if needed).
Place these in the com.examly.springapp.model and com.examly.springapp.repository packages as per convention.
description: Defines the core database schema, relationships, and required custom queries supporting all business logic and endpoints.

step: Implement Freelancer and Project Services for Business Logic
sub_steps: Create FreelancerService with core methods: getAllFreelancers, getFreelancerById, createFreelancer (with validation and error aggregation), findFreelancersBySkill, etc.
Create ProjectService with corresponding methods: getAllProjects, getProjectById, createProject (with validation and error aggregation), assignFreelancerToProject, findProjectsByStatus, etc.
Add error handling for not found and validation errors, including custom Exception classes if needed (e.g., ResourceNotFoundException).
description: Services encapsulate the main business logic, separating validation, error handling, and repository interaction away from controllers.

step: Implement REST Controllers for Freelancer and Project APIs with Validation and Error Handling
sub_steps: Create FreelancerController and ProjectController under com.examly.springapp.controller.

Implement required endpoints for each as per question (GET/POST/PUT with validation and clear error message formats, validation aggregation, correct status codes, matching the response structures in example scenarios).
Implement validation using @Valid and BindingResult (collect field errors for failed validation), manual checks where necessary (e.g., for status enum, budget, date logic).
On error conditions, return JSON error format as specified.
Add CORS configuration (using @CrossOrigin or WebMvcConfigurer) to allow frontend communication.
Refer to test cases and example scenarios to ensure all behaviors are covered.
description: Implements RESTful API endpoints, precise input validation, proper error handling and response codes as per requirements and test cases.

step: Implement Required Backend Test Cases (JUnit/Mockito) in Spring Boot
sub_steps: For testCreateFreelancer, testGetFreelancerById, testCreateProject, testAssignFreelancerToProject, testFindProjectsByStatus: create or update *Test.java files to cover all positive and negative scenarios, using @WebMvcTest, @MockBean for services/repos, and MockMvc.
Mock repository/service beans as needed to return expected objects for test coverage.
Verify response status, body, and proper error messages/structures for all paths (success and failure cases). Match error formats exactly.
Ensure test isolation (reset mocks per test), no manual cleanup() calls.
Map each test to the requirement/component/feature it exercises.
description: Implements all backend test cases for controller logic, error handling, validation, and integration, supporting robust TDD coverage as per Test Cases JSON.
